newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: SEOUL STOCKS END LOWER ON BLUE CHIP SELLING.
newsitem.headline: SEOUL STOCKS END LOWER ON BLUE CHIP SELLING.

text.p: Seoul stocks closed lower on Thursday as institutional investors took profits on recent blue chip gains, brokers said.
"Stocks that weigh heavily on the index took a big hit on institutional profit-taking," said Park Joo-chang of Daewoo Securities.
Brokers expected the consolidation to continue on Saturday. The market is closed on Friday for the Liberation Day.
The composite stock index closed down 6.95 points to 755.78 with 35.7 million shares changing hands.
Despite the index drop, risers led losers 389 to 377.
"Samsung Electronics and Korea Electric Power led the index decline although there were similar number of advancing and declining stocks," said Park Ki-pyong of Hanyang Securities.
Samsung Electronics lost 1,200 won to 73,500, KEPCO fell 1,100 to 25,700, Pohang Iron and Steel dropped 800 to 61,100 and SK Telecom shed 3,000 to 500,000.
Samsung was also hit by a poor first-half earnings report. Its interim net profit fell to 123.2 billion won against 453.4 billion a year ago.
"Samsung took a blow from falling profits while LG Electronics gained on strong earnings," said Park.
LG Electronics closed up 600 won to 20,000.
The securities sub-index dropped 1.84 percent to 1,286.37 and insurance sub-index lost 1.58 percent to 3,739.36.
Shares of Korea First Bank closed up 150 to 3,640 after opening at their upper daily limit of 3,760 as investors accumulated shares on hopes of government help.
It was the most heavily traded stock with 783,170 shares changing hands.
The finance ministry said on Wednesday it was considering ways to help Korea First Bank which has been hit by loan defaults by big conglomerates.
Possible government steps included special loans from the central bank, rights issue offerings or lower provisions for non-performing loans.
"Korea First Bank shares are likely to fall back unless the special loan is provided," said Park of Daewoo.
